BiblicalUsage: Erēmía is solitude — the lonely place, the wilderness where no one lives. Jesus feeds the multitude in a desert place; Paul is in perils in the wilderness; and Hebrews says the world was not worthy of those who wandered in deserts. It is the word for being alone with God — or alone without Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe erēmía is the word for the lonely places God uses: the wilderness where Jesus feeds, and the desert where His people wander. I hold that solitude with God is never truly alone.
